name: Pneumatosis Intestinalis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Radiologic and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Pneumatosis Intestinalis

criteria.description: Presence of gas cysts within the intestinal wall on imaging studies (X-ray, CT scan)
Gastrointestinal symptoms such as abdominal pain, distension, or diarrhea
Exclusion of bowel ischemia or necrosis by clinical, laboratory, and imaging evaluation
Endoscopic visualization of submucosal gas cysts if performed

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of gas cysts within the intestinal wall on imaging plus exclusion of bowel ischemia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires correlation of imaging findings with clinical presentation and exclusion of life-threatening causes.

pathognomonic.notes: Detected radiologically; hallmark of the condition

laboratory: Possible leukocytosis if secondary infection or ischemia present
Elevated lactate in cases of bowel ischemia
imaging: Radiographic evidence of gas cysts within the bowel wall on abdominal X-ray or CT scan
CT scan showing intramural gas with or without portal venous gas
other: Endoscopic visualization of submucosal gas cysts
Histopathology showing gas-filled cysts in the submucosa or subserosa

distinguishingFeatures: Severe abdominal pain out of proportion to exam
Absence of benign gas cysts on imaging
Fever and systemic signs of infection
Positive stool cultures or pathogen identification
Diffuse bowel wall thickening without gas cysts
Chronic diarrhea with blood and mucus

redFlags: Signs of bowel ischemia or necrosis
references: Ho LM, Paulson EK, Thompson WM. Pneumatosis intestinalis in the adult: benign to life-threatening causes. AJR Am J Roentgenol. 2007;188(6):1604-1613.
Koss LG. Pneumatosis cystoides intestinalis: a review. Am J Pathol. 1952;28(3): 455-479.
St Peter SD, Abbas MA, Kelly KA. The spectrum of pneumatosis intestinalis. Arch Surg. 2003;138(1):68-75.
